title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered 102 and headed 'IX', from Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §9.2. It sets up the monodromy pairing for an abelian variety with semistable reduction. It is a stray leaf in the folder: it has nothing to do with the divided-power de Rham notes on the neighbouring pages, which concern graded modules and truncation functors.

Setting. K is a discretely valued field with residue field k, and A_K is an abelian variety with semistable reduction. A'_K is the dual abelian variety. U = T_ℓ(A(K̄)), V = U^I is the part fixed by inertia, and W ⊂ V is the toric part, i.e. the part coming from the torus T_0 in the special fibre of the Néron model. U', V', W' are the same objects for A'.

Step 1 (orthogonality theorem, SGA 7 IX 5.2). Under the Weil pairing U × U' → Z_ℓ(1), the annihilator of V is W (and likewise for A'). Hence (U/V)^∨ ≅ W'(-1).

Step 2 (factoring the inertia action). Semistability makes inertia act unipotently: σ ↦ σ − 1 gives a map U → U/V → W. This action factors through the tame ℓ-quotient I(ℓ) ≅ Z_ℓ(1). So it becomes a canonical map u: Z_ℓ(1) → Hom(U/V, W) = W' ⊗ W(-1), equivalently an element u ∈ W' ⊗ W(-2).

Step 3 (identifying W and W'). W and W' are the K̄-points of the twisted constant ℓ-adic sheaves T_ℓ(A^0)^t and T_ℓ(A'^0)^t, whose special fibres are T_ℓ(T_0) and T_ℓ(T'_0). Write M, M' for the character groups of T_0 = D(M) and T'_0 = D(M'). Then W ≅ M^∨ ⊗ Z_ℓ(1) and W' ≅ M'^∨ ⊗ Z_ℓ(1).

Step 4 (the pairing). The Tate twists cancel, so u lands in M'^∨ ⊗ M^∨ ⊗ Z_ℓ, i.e. it is a bilinear form M × M' → Z_ℓ. This is Grothendieck's monodromy pairing. On the following page of SGA 7 it is shown to be Z-valued and non-degenerate, and it is related to the valuation of Raynaud's/Mumford's period lattice and to component groups.
errors: The second line of (9.2.7) as typed reads 'W' ≃ T_ℓ(T_o(k̄)) ≃ M'⊗Z_ℓ(1)'. Two corrections are needed: T_o should be T'_o, and M' should be the dual lattice M'^∨ (check missing), by symmetry with the first line and with T_ℓ(D(M)) = Hom(M, Z_ℓ(1)).
The first line, 'T_ℓ(T_o)(k̄))', has an unbalanced parenthesis. These are typing slips only and do not affect the mathematics.

ideas.what: Orthogonality theorem: V^⊥ = W under the Weil pairing, giving (U/V)^∨ ≅ W'(-1).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem (fixed part versus toric part)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX (1967-69, publ. 1972)

ideas.what: The inertia action factors through Z_ℓ(1) and gives u ∈ W'⊗W(-2), which reinterprets as a bilinear form on the character groups M × M'.
Identification of the toric part of the Tate module with the cocharacter lattice ⊗ Z_ℓ(1).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX (§9.2, monodromy pairing). It was simply misfiled among the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. Its content is classical and fully credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: Second line of (9.2.7): the image reads 'W' ≃ T_ℓ(T_o(k̄)) ≃ M'⊗Z_ℓ(1)'. Mathematically it should be T_ℓ(T'_o)(k̄) ≃ M'^∨⊗Z_ℓ(1); this is a typo in the original typescript, not a transcription error.
The page is not part of cote 136's de Rham notes: it is p.102 of the SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript (archive stamp 420).
